name: the-dock-side-switches-from-the-frontend
description:
the frontend's own dock control switches the side and the pane re-lays-out. Reachability was settled by the sibling scenario; this presses the control.

The pane's dock-state VLOG already carries strategy.bounds(), so side-versus-bottom is readable from the bounds change alone with no new instrumentation.

actions.note: let the space and its single tab render
ssh-launched Atrium is not frontmost on a clean snapshot; without this the keystroke lands in Finder (traffic-routing learned this the hard way)
open DevTools on the active tab
DevTools frontend is a full WebContents load - generous on purpose, the dock VLOG only fires once UpdateDockedDevtoolsForPane runs with a non-null GetInTabWebContents
arming read: proves the frontend answers before anything is pressed

actions.expression: (() => { const find = (root, depth) => { if (depth > 8) return null; for (const el of root.querySelectorAll('*')) {   if (el.shadowRoot) { const hit = find(el.shadowRoot, depth + 1); if (hit) return hit; }   const l = (el.getAttribute && el.getAttribute('aria-label')) || '';   if (/customize and control/i.test(l)) return el; } return null; }; const btn = find(document, 0); if (!btn) return 'no menu button'; btn.click(); return 'clicked'; })()
actions.note: presses the menu that holds Dock side. Returns what it did rather than nothing, so a run where the button vanished is distinguishable from one where the click did nothing.

actions.expression: (() => { const hits = []; const walk = (root, depth) => { if (depth > 10) return; for (const el of root.querySelectorAll('*')) {   if (el.shadowRoot) walk(el.shadowRoot, depth + 1);   const l = (el.getAttribute && el.getAttribute('aria-label')) ||              (el.getAttribute && el.getAttribute('title')) || '';   if (/dock|undock/i.test(l)) hits.push(l); } }; walk(document, 0); return [...new Set(hits)].join(' | ') || 'none'; })()
actions.note: the dock choices the open menu offers, matched on aria-label and title. textContent finds nothing because they are icon buttons - the same reason the menu button itself was only findable by label.

actions.expression: (() => { const find = (root, depth) => { if (depth > 10) return null; for (const el of root.querySelectorAll('*')) {   if (el.shadowRoot) { const h = find(el.shadowRoot, depth + 1); if (h) return h; }   const l = (el.getAttribute && el.getAttribute('aria-label')) || '';   if (/^dock to bottom$/i.test(l.trim())) return el; } return null; }; const item = find(document, 0); if (!item) return 'not offered'; item.click(); return 'clicked'; })()
actions.note: Switch the dock side from the frontend's own control

assertions.note: the arming read, checked first: without it every result below could be a blind zero
the menu button was found and pressed
the Dock to bottom item was offered and pressed

assertions.label: the-pane-relaid-out-underneath
assertions.note: The PANE re-lays-out, read from the dock-state line's own strategy.bounds(). A bottom dock has a different bounds shape from a side dock, which is what comment #5 predicted would make this assertable with no new instrumentation.
